_note: Generated from prompts/*.md by scripts/build-prompt-index.mjs — edit the markdown, then regenerate. Model-agnostic: plain text for any chat AI (Gemini, Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude) or any program.
safe_prompt_rule: Remove sensitive data first, review output before sharing, and keep a human in charge of every decision.

categories.name: Bid And Opportunity Support
categories.description: These prompts are for early, non-sensitive bid or opportunity support. They are not a substitute for official pricing, procurement, legal, sales, or customer commitments.

categories.name: Customer and Contractor Communication
categories.description: These prompts help draft professional, empathetic communication for customers and contractors. **Never include real customer names, tracking numbers, addresses, or delivery photos.**

categories.name: Daily Operations
categories.description: These prompts cover the core daily workflow of a FedEx FEC supervisor or manager: shift briefs, handoffs, escalations, and after-action reviews. All prompts use scrubbed, non-sensitive data only.

categories.name: Linehaul and Routing
categories.description: Linehaul (long-distance transport between hubs and stations) and P&D routing are core FedEx operations. These prompts help managers plan, communicate, and problem-solve without exposing real route manifests, carrier contracts, or facility security details.

categories.name: Peak Season and Surge Planning
categories.description: Peak season (roughly October through January) is the highest-stakes period for FedEx operations. These prompts help managers plan, communicate, and debrief without exposing real volume forecasts, staffing numbers, or customer data.

categories.name: Safety and Compliance
categories.description: FedEx's first value is **Safety Above All**. These prompts help managers draft safety-related communication without ever including real employee names, incident locations, or injury details in unapproved AI tools.

prompts.title: Opportunity Intake
prompts.text:
Act as an FEC supervisor or manager helping organize a possible opportunity.

Opportunity summary:
[Paste non-sensitive summary.]

Return:
- What the opportunity appears to be
- Who should review it
- Information needed before a go/no-go decision
- Operational constraints to check
- Customer or legal commitments to avoid making too early
- Recommended next step

Do not invent pricing, capacity, service commitments, or approval status.

prompts.title: Bid Readiness Checklist
prompts.text:

[Paste description.]

Return a checklist grouped by:

- Operational capacity
- Staffing

- Data needed

Flag anything that needs official approval.

prompts.title: Go / No-Go Brief

prompts.title: Service Alert Draft (Generic)
prompts.text:
Draft a generic service alert for customers in a affected area.

Area: [General region, e.g., "Denver metro area"]
Issue: [General description, e.g., "severe weather may cause delays"]

- What customers should expect
- How to get updates (generic: "Track your shipment at fedex.com")

Under 150 words. Do not include real tracking numbers, names, or addresses.
placeholders: [General description, e.g., "severe weather may cause delays"]

prompts.title: Customer Escalation Response Draft

placeholders: [e.g., missed delivery window, damaged package, incorrect address]
[General type, e.g., redelivery, claim process, manager callback]

prompts.title: Daily Manager Brief
prompts.text:
Act as a FedEx FEC supervisor or manager preparing a concise daily brief for your station or hub.

Context (scrubbed — no real names, addresses, tracking numbers, or package counts):
[Paste non-sensitive shift notes, volume ranges, staffing notes, weather summary,
equipment notes, and known constraints.]

Create a daily brief with:
- Top 5 priorities for this shift
- Risks to watch (weather, road, equipment, staffing)
- Sort hub / P&D / linehaul coordination notes
- Decisions needed and who should make them
- Owner and next step for each item

Rules:
- Do not invent facts.
- Put unclear items under "Needs verification."
- Keep it under 300 words.
- Include a safety reminder.
placeholders:
[Paste non-sensitive shift notes, volume ranges, staffing notes, weather summary,
equipment notes, and known constraints.]

prompts.title: Shift Handoff
prompts.text:
Turn these non-sensitive notes into a shift handoff for the incoming FedEx FEC supervisor or manager.

Outgoing shift: [Day/Evening/Night]
Incoming shift: [Day/Evening/Night]
Tone: direct, calm, and action-oriented

Notes (scrubbed):
[Paste notes. Remove all real names, addresses, tracking numbers, and package details.]

Return:
1. What changed since the last handoff
2. What is still open
3. High-risk items (safety, customer, linehaul)
4. Who owns each next step (roles, not names)
5. What to check first in the next shift
6. One safety reminder
placeholders: [Paste notes. Remove all real names, addresses, tracking numbers, and package details.]

prompts.title: Escalation Summary
prompts.text:
Summarize this issue for an escalation to senior management or a support team.

Use neutral language. Do not blame people. Flag assumptions.

prompts.title: After-Action Review

Return:

- Closing: "Safety Above All. Questions?"

Under 150 words. No real names, package counts, or facility security details.
placeholders: [e.g., all belts operational, chute 3 down for repair]
[e.g., late feeder arrival expected, overflow lot in use]

prompts.title: End-of-Shift Closeout Checklist
prompts.text:
Create an end-of-shift closeout checklist for a FedEx FEC supervisor or manager.

Shift: [Day/Evening/Night]

Return a checklist with:

placeholders: [e.g., "higher than typical Tuesday", "unexpected drop in outbound"]
[e.g., weather, local event, system issue, carrier delay]

prompts.title: Feeder Delay Communication
prompts.text:
Draft a communication about a feeder/linehaul delay for station awareness.

General route: [e.g., "eastbound mountain corridor"]

Return:

prompts.title: Alternate Routing Recommendation
prompts.text:

Return:
- Pros and cons of each alternate (distance, time, risk, capacity)

- Trigger points for switching back to primary
- Communication needed (roles, not names)
- Safety considerations

Label all times and distances as estimates. Add: "Verify routes with carrier dispatch and official road sources."
placeholders: [General description, e.g., "I-70 westbound through Vail Pass"]

prompts.title: Pre-Peak Contingency Brief
prompts.text:

Keep under 400 words. Use placeholders for any specific numbers.

prompts.title: Daily Surge Checklist
